answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated fraud. A signal from one account earns little; repeated claims gain weight only after distinct, stake-backed identities support them over time. The quill records each stake and penalty in a public ledger, while a crystal-clear audit trail lets honest agents challenge suspicious clusters. A sybil attacker must lock up more capital per identity and risks losing it, making scale costly rather than free.
